breakHistory.change: This freeze stopped hashing the video instruction plan directly and started hashing the video freeze artifact instead. The artifact entry 'video instruction plan' (texas/tx-law-of-agency-30-v1/video-instruction-plan.md) is replaced by 'video plan freeze' (texas/tx-law-of-agency-30-v1/video-plan-freeze.json), written by the new scripts/freeze-loa-video-plan.mjs under the id LOA-VIDEO-PLAN-FREEZE-2026-08-30-v2. That video freeze hashes the plan, the three production files, the three caption .vtt files, the held IABS 1-2 form and OC.1101 statute, the source inventory, the three block maps the videos name, the new validator, and the block-map generator core. Two artifacts also gained content at the same moment: the video plan itself was corrected to plan v2 (nine narration repairs, one statutory repair, seven coordinate corrections and one duration inconsistency, all previously stranded in an unhashed addendum), and the addendum was marked SUPERSEDED review history.
breakHistory.reason: The structural cause of a deadlock, removed. A video plan is not curriculum, and correcting a video should never require breaking a curriculum freeze — but while this freeze hashed the plan directly, it did. That is not hypothetical: an earlier pass found real defects in the three video packages (the worst dropped 'unless required to do so by law' from a confidentiality rule while the highlight box was showing the student that very exception), edited the plan to record them, saw this freeze report drift, correctly reversed the edit byte for byte, and parked the corrections in an unhashed addendum. The result was a hashed canonical plan carrying known defects and an unhashed file carrying the fixes — fine as review history, not acceptable as a production package, because a renderer consulting the canonical files would have reproduced the defects. Indirection fixes the cause: the curriculum freeze still pins the video state exactly, because any change to any video artifact changes the video freeze and therefore this hash, but it pins it through a stable pointer that the video freeze owns.
breakHistory.whyTheFreezeIdIS_Bumped: Because the artifact changed. content-freeze.json's artifacts map loses one key and gains another, with a different path and a different hash. Re-taking under v3 would make an id denote two byte-states, and an id that denotes two byte-states is not an identifier — anyone verifying against v3 could not tell which of the two they held. That reasoning has already been applied once in this history, to the v2 -> v3 bump, and it applies here for the same reason and with less room for argument, since this time the artifacts map itself is structurally different.
breakHistory.curriculumUnchanged: All twelve module sha256 values are identical to v3's. So are the LOA-1 outline, the source register, the quotation ledger, the claim audit, the time evidence, the misconception checks, the time budget, the structural generator and the salvage audit. The only difference between the v3 and v4 artifacts is the video entry and the freeze id.
breakHistory.foundBy: the consolidation pass, reading the addendum's own account of why it existed
breakHistory.classOfDefect: structural — the freeze boundary was drawn in the wrong place, so a correct edit to a video could not land

breakHistory.reason: The subsection letter was wrong. The held rule file prints no subsection letters, so they are derived by ordinal position; that derivation is anchored by the rule's own internal cross-references to 'subsection (e)' for delegation and 'subsection (h)' for records, and it puts the listings rule at (f) and the sponsored agent's advertising compliance at (g). Modules 01, 02 and 09 all cite (f); module 04 was the outlier. A student looking up § 535.2(g) would have found the advertising rule.

breakHistory.whyTheMechanicalAuditMissedIt: The claim auditor resolves '22 TAC § 535.2' to its held file and verifies the section is present. It does not verify a subsection letter, because the held file carries none. This is a known coverage limit of the tool, not a lapse in its operation, and it is why a human-scale read of the corpus still finds things enumeration cannot.
breakHistory.classOfDefect: citation-only — the quoted text is verbatim and the proposition is correct; only the subsection identifier was wrong. Nothing downstream mis-taught a rule.

identifiedNotTaught.unit: Federal and State Law Relating to Conduct
identifiedNotTaught.passage: the closing sentence of the fair-housing exemptions passage in T10U2, which tells the student where the held subchapter stops
identifiedNotTaught.whyItCannotReceiveAMechanicalPass: The mechanical check asks whether a cited section is present in the held source. This section is not present, because Subchapter C of Property Code ch. 301 as held runs from 301.041 to 301.044 and stops. A check that verifies presence cannot pass a citation to something absent, and it should not: the correct outcome is to surface it for review, which is what happened.
identifiedNotTaught.humanReviewedDisposition: NOT A DEFECT. The citation appears once, inside a sentence whose whole purpose is to tell the student that this section was not held and is not taught. No proposition is asserted from it, no rule is stated on its authority, and no assessment item can reference it.
identifiedNotTaught.howItGotIntoTheCourse: My authoring brief for module 10 listed the Texas exemptions as sections 301.041 through 301.045. That range was mine and it was wrong. The author checked the held statute, found the subchapter ends at 301.044, and recorded the discrepancy in the module rather than quietly writing to the range I had given. That is the behaviour the sourcing rule is for.
evidenceItIsNotASourcingOrLegalDefect: The held source texas/trec-sources/statutes/PR.301.htm contains Sec. 301.041 CERTAIN SALES AND RENTALS EXEMPTED, Sec. 301.042 RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATION, PRIVATE CLUB, AND APPRAISAL EXEMPTION, Sec. 301.043 HOUSING FOR ELDERLY EXEMPTED and Sec. 301.044 EFFECT ON OTHER LAW, and no Sec. 301.045.
All four exemptions that do exist are taught in T10U2 in required prose.

The course text reads: 'Subchapter C of the chapter as held runs from 301.041 to 301.044 and stops there. A 301.045 was not held for this course and is not taught here; the four exemptions above are the whole of the subchapter as read.'
The claim carries status IDENTIFIED_NOT_TAUGHT, the classification the audit gives a citation the course itself disclaims, and it is counted in the denominator rather than excluded from it.
